minutes.headline: Open Space Committee voted to recommend the town waive its right of first refusal on three Chapter 61 lots, with conditions.
minutes.summary: A special remote meeting, requested by the select board, took up the right of first refusal on three lots on Kilburn Street and Leominster Road that are being converted out of Chapter 61. The committee recommended not exercising the right. It added a request that the planning board forward Chapter 61 notices to it and check Chapter 61 enrollment on subdivisions. The committee also dropped its August meeting and kept September 11.

attendees.role: new planning administrator (addressed, said to be on the call)

votes.motion: Recommend that the town waive its right of first refusal on the three Chapter 61 lots. Also recommend that the planning board forward any Chapter 61 withdrawal notices to the committee in a timely way. Also recommend that the planning board confirm with the assessor that any parcel over five acres coming in for subdivision is not enrolled in Chapter 61.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Brandon, Eric, Glen, Mary aye, and the chair also aye)
passed (Brandon, Mary and Glenn aye; Eric's microphone was out; the chair said four of five voted)

decisions.decision: The chair will ask the new planning administrator to add a quick Chapter 61 enrollment check to the checklist for incoming filings.
The August 14 meeting is dropped. The September 11 meeting is kept for now.
The chair will ask the Parks Commission chair about the committee's new member from Parks.
Brandon will send notes and the chair will pass them to the select board, which meets next Tuesday.

what_happened.line: The Open Space Committee voted by roll call, all ayes, to recommend that the town waive its right of first refusal on three Chapter 61 lots.
The same motion asked the planning board to forward Chapter 61 withdrawal notices to the committee and to confirm with the assessor that subdivided parcels over five acres are not enrolled.
Members discussed the value of the right of first refusal, the reduced taxes owners pay under Chapter 61B, short statutory timelines and the lack of notice.
The chair will ask the new planning administrator to add a Chapter 61 enrollment check to the filing checklist.
The August 14 meeting was dropped and September 11 kept for now; notes will go to the select board, which meets next Tuesday.

why_it_matters: Chapter 61 land taken out of that program can be bought by the town first, and a recommendation to waive means the committee is not advising the town to buy these lots.

The request for timely notices and an enrollment check on subdivisions targets how the town learns of such conversions, which are on short statutory timelines, so the next lot may not reach the committee in time without it.
